evidence.claim: The AI optical-interconnect branch is a valid Layer 3 research area because the provided Layer 2 catalysts identify 800G-to-1.6T optical transition and possible co-packaged optics commercialization as drivers that can shift bottlenecks among InP wafers, lasers, photodiodes, optical manufacturing services, and module assembly.

The provided external context states that the commercial-grade precision substrate supplier base for 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers numbers fewer than six companies worldwide, supporting high supplier-scarcity scores for InP substrate candidates.
evidence.source: THE FORTY-YEAR EDGE THAT AI CANNOT FUNCTION WITHOUT

evidence.claim: The provided external context states that one core product line tied to AI data-center demand nearly tripled year over year and had backlog equivalent to a full year of production at the current quarterly run rate. This supports the hypothesis that customers may be shifting from spot orders to allocation-securing commitments.
evidence.source: THE FORTY-YEAR EDGE THAT AI CANNOT FUNCTION WITHOUT

evidence.claim: The provided Layer 2 context frames new orders for MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, and other compound semiconductor photonics tools as a hypothesis-level early signal that optical component suppliers are adding AI data-center capacity.
The provided Layer 2 context states that OSATs can act as relief valves when foundry advanced-package capacity and test flows become constrained.

The provided external context states that Broadcom reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $22.19 billion, up 48% year over year, and semiconductor revenue of $15.0 billion, up 79% year over year, driven by custom AI accelerators and AI networking.
evidence.source: Signals from SEC Filings — Tech Supply Chain | InvestReport.ai

evidence.claim: The provided external context frames AI capex as a stack where useful research follows dollars layer by layer and asks where supply is hardest to add. This supports prioritizing suppliers, tools, substrates, optical manufacturing, packaging, power, and other second-order nodes rather than ranking by popularity.
evidence.source: The Companies Behind the AI Supply Chain - Ankur Gupta

memory_update.content: For AI optical-interconnect chunks, prioritize substrate and tool suppliers above obvious optical reference leaders when there is evidence of supplier scarcity, backlog conversion, qualification cycles, and customer allocation behavior.

AXTI, VECO, FN, and 6239.TW should advance to the next Serenity evidence-check layer; COHR, LITE, AVGO, and ALAB should remain reference benchmarks; ALMU should remain speculative-shadow pending commercial validation.

Downgrade the InP/optical chokepoint thesis if 800G/1.6T demand does not translate into sustained backlog, lead-time expansion, customer commitments, capacity utilization, pricing support, or margin improvement at substrate, tool, component, and optical manufacturing suppliers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether InP backlog converts into revenue without export-permit delays, yield issues, customer de-qualification, capacity overbuild, or pricing compression.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The strongest current signal comes from third-party thematic reporting rather than directly cited filings in the provided context. The key gap is direct confirmation from AXTI disclosures on InP revenue mix, AI/datacom customer exposure, backlog duration, capacity utilization, lead times, customer commitments, and pricing.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AXT ranks first because the candidate thesis maps directly to a narrow substrate-level bottleneck: InP wafers for 800G and 1.6T optical devices used in AI data-center photonics. The external context claims that commercial-grade precision substrate supply for 800G/1.6T optical transceivers is limited to fewer than six global suppliers and that one product line tied to AI data-center demand grew nearly threefold year over year, with backlog equivalent to roughly a full year of current production. That evidence, if verified in company filings and customer/order language, fits the Serenity pattern of scarce suppliers, long qualification cycles, and customer allocation behavior.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is screened as a niche compound-semiconductor substrate and materials company rather than as an AI networking or optical-module beneficiary. That classification gap creates a plausible discovery edge versus more obvious optical component or transceiver names.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether 2026 InP equipment orders represent one-time capacity catch-up or a durable multi-year photonics capex cycle.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need direct company evidence showing order growth tied specifically to InP photonics, datacom lasers, optical transceiver supply chains, or AI data-center customers rather than broader compound-semiconductor cycles.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Veeco ranks highly because it is one step upstream from the optical-component bottleneck. If InP lasers, photodiodes, and other compound photonics devices are capacity constrained, MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, and related manufacturing tools can become early capex signals. The provided Layer 2 catalyst explicitly frames new orders for compound semiconductor photonics tools as a hypothesis-level leading indicator of AI optical capacity expansion.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is often grouped into general semiconductor or compound-semiconductor equipment rather than mapped specifically to AI data-center optical interconnect capacity. That creates a potentially underappreciated link between 800G/1.6T optical demand and tool orders.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify AI datacom revenue mix, backlog, customer concentration, Thailand capacity expansion, 800G/1.6T production language, and gross-margin impact.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The key gap is customer and product-level specificity. Need evidence that AI datacom optical manufacturing, not legacy telecom or other precision manufacturing, is driving incremental revenue and margin.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Fabrinet ranks third because specialized optical manufacturing can become a qualification and ramp bottleneck when AI clusters drive 800G and 1.6T transceiver volumes. The candidate has a clear test path through AI datacom revenue mix, backlog, Thailand capacity, customer concentration, 800G/1.6T production language, and margin progression.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is commonly labeled as contract manufacturing or precision optical manufacturing rather than as a direct AI infrastructure bottleneck. Its AI exposure may be hidden inside customer programs and production ramps rather than branded end-products.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify IDM outsourcing volumes, price increases, FOPLP customer validation, AI/HPC packaging revenue mix, yield progress, and CPO commercialization timing.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Current support is hypothesis-level. Need direct evidence of AI/HPC packaging revenue, HBM-related spillover, customer outsourcing commitments, advanced packaging yield progress, and pricing or utilization improvement.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Powertech is prioritized as an underfollowed memory-backend and packaging-capacity beneficiary. The hypothesis is that AI-driven HBM demand crowds out conventional DRAM and NAND backend work at memory IDMs, pushing outsourcing volume toward third-party OSATs. This is less directly proven than the InP/optics lane, but it fits the Serenity search for second-order capacity relief valves.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It sits one step away from obvious HBM leaders and may be screened as a Taiwan memory packaging/test OSAT rather than as an AI packaging-capacity beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify datacom AI growth, InP fab utilization, customer prepayments, long-term supply agreements, constrained product lines, and margin impact.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need company-specific confirmation of AI datacenter mix, constrained product lines, customer commitments, and whether InP capacity is actually tight enough to affect pricing, lead times, or margins.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Lumentum is a useful benchmark for InP-dependent optical devices and datacenter optical components. It has more direct product relevance than broad AI infrastructure names, but it is less underfollowed than substrate or tool suppliers. It should be used to benchmark whether bottlenecks are occurring at the component, laser, photodiode, or transceiver level.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Less obscure than substrate/tool suppliers, but it may still be treated as a cyclical optical-component company rather than as a constrained AI photonics-capacity name.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track InP capacity, 800G/1.6T order visibility, customer prepayments, lead times, gross-margin mix, and whether bottlenecks shift from substrates to lasers, photodiodes, packaging, or modules.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current direct evidence that AI datacenter optical demand is creating sustained margin, backlog, and lead-time pressure rather than a temporary order surge already reflected in expectations.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Coherent is a reference leader for AI datacenter optical connectivity, InP device capacity, transceiver ramps, and photonics supply tightness. It ranks below underfollowed names because attention is already high and the discovery edge is lower, but it remains important for validating the broader optical-capacity thesis.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed in 2026; included as a reference anchor to benchmark smaller substrate, equipment, and alternative photonics candidates.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify AI customer mix, hyperscaler concentration, design wins, active electrical cable ramps, margin sustainability, and competitive response.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need stronger evidence tying revenue growth to specific AI cluster deployments, durable hyperscaler design wins, attach rates, and competitive differentiation versus other connectivity suppliers.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Credo remains relevant to the AI bandwidth bottleneck through high-speed connectivity semiconductors, retimers, and active electrical cables. It ranks below the optical substrate/tool/manufacturing names because the candidate claim is more general and the provided evidence base is weaker for a specific chokepoint.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It can be screened as a narrow connectivity-chip company rather than as an AI cluster bandwidth enabler, though its attention level has likely increased as AI connectivity became a better-known theme.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify AI semiconductor revenue mix, hyperscaler customer concentration, custom ASIC backlog, and whether inference silicon growth is already fully priced.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The main research issue is not whether Broadcom has AI exposure, but whether smaller suppliers tied to Broadcom-like custom ASIC and networking growth offer more underfollowed, purer bottleneck exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Broadcom is included as a demand anchor for custom AI accelerators, AI networking, substrates, packaging, test, and connectivity suppliers. The external context states that Broadcom reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $22.19 billion, up 48% year over year, with semiconductor revenue of $15.0 billion, up 79% year over year, driven by custom AI accelerators and AI networking. However, it is a mega-cap reference name rather than an underfollowed discovery candidate.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a reference leader for the custom AI silicon and networking branch of the supply chain.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify customer concentration, AI platform attach rates, pricing durability, and whether market expectations already assume sustained exponential growth.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that incremental AI platform attach rates and pricing durability exceed expectations already embedded in market attention.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Astera Labs is relevant as a reference-growth supplier in AI server connectivity, PCIe/CXL retimers, and high-speed data movement. It ranks lower because it is already highly associated with AI infrastructure growth, which reduces underfollowed discovery value and raises the burden of proving mispricing.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not meaningfully underfollowed within the AI connectivity theme; better used as a reference comparable for smaller or less obvious connectivity suppliers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify commercial qualification, production purchase orders, customer agreements, revenue composition, manufacturing readiness, cash runway, and any documented relationship with optical supply-chain customers.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The core gap is commercial proof. Need signed customer agreements, production purchase orders, qualified products, manufacturing yield data, and adequate cash runway before it can move beyond speculative-shadow status.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Aeluma has high theoretical discovery value as a speculative alternative architecture if native InP wafer/device capacity constrains AI optical interconnect supply. However, it ranks last despite a higher raw discovery score because commercial validation, production readiness, customer evidence, and financial durability are not established in the provided context.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a micro-cap III-V-on-silicon photonics platform company outside mainstream AI infrastructure screens, with limited commercial validation.

summary: This Layer 3 ranking prioritizes underfollowed AI infrastructure chokepoints in optical interconnects, InP substrates, photonics manufacturing tools, specialized optical manufacturing, and memory/backend packaging. The highest research priority goes to names with direct exposure to capacity constraints, testable order/backlog or qualification evidence, and plausible public-market mispricing from being classified outside the obvious AI GPU/custom-silicon lane. Reference leaders are retained only as benchmarks, not as the main discovery targets.
